remaining_gaps: Own-terms ending of the Task Force clauses cannot be fixed from held evidence. Section 2(f) of EO 13995 provides that, unless extended by the President, the Task Force terminates within 30 days of accomplishing the objectives set forth in the order, including delivery of the report and recommendations, or 2 years from the date of the order, whichever comes first. The Task Force clauses therefore ended on a date no later than two years after 2021-01-21 unless extended, which is before the 2025-01-20 revocation by EO 14148, and possibly earlier if the objectives were accomplished sooner. No held source dates the accomplishment of the objectives or the delivery of the report, and no held source shows an extension. Missing source: a held official record dating the Task Force report and recommendations (or its disbandment) and showing whether the President extended it.

Own-terms ending of the Task Force clause cannot be fixed from held evidence. Section 5(e) of EO 14011 provides that the Task Force terminates 30 days after it provides its final report to the President under section 4(c)(iv), so the Task Force clauses may have ended before the 2025-01-20 revocation by EO 14148. No held source records whether or when the final report was provided. Missing source: a held official record dating the final report to the President (or showing none was provided before 2025-01-20).

Own-terms ending of the Commission clauses cannot be fixed from held evidence. Section 5 of EO 14023 provides that the Commission terminates 30 days after it submits its report to the President, so the Commission clauses may have ended well before the 2025-01-20 revocation by EO 14148. No held source records the date the Commission submitted its report. Missing source: a held official record dating the Commission report submission to the President.

Own-terms ending of the Climate Change Support Office clause cannot be fixed from held evidence. Section 1(e) of EO 14027 provides that the CCSO terminates at the end of the maximum period permitted by section 3161(a)(1) of title 5, United States Code, unless sooner terminated by the Secretary, so a date earlier than the 2025-01-20 revocation may exist. The packet holds no text of 5 U.S.C. 3161 and no record of when the CCSO was established or terminated. Missing source: the text of 5 U.S.C. 3161 as in force from 2021 and a record dating the CCSO establishment or earlier termination by the Secretary.

Own-terms ending of one interim clause cannot be fixed from held evidence. Section 19(b) of EO 14074 directs the Attorney General to develop and publish accreditation-body standards within 240 days and provides that, pending the development of such standards, the Attorney General shall maintain the current requirements related to accreditation. That interim command ended on its own terms when the standards were developed, which may precede the 2025-01-20 revocation by EO 14148, and no held source shows whether or when the Attorney General published the standards. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-28 an interval is claimed only when evidence shows the event occurred, so the clause cannot be assigned an end date. Missing source: a held official record (Department of Justice publication or Federal Register notice) dating the standards, or showing none were published before 2025-01-20. The packet inventory (180 clauses) and the whole-order revocation by section 2(vv) of EO 14148 on 2025-01-20 were otherwise consistent; EO 14110 cites sections 2(b), 3 and 13(e) of EO 14074 only as cross-references and is not an amendment or end.

Own-terms ending of three interim clauses cannot be fixed from held evidence. Section 4.2(b) provides that, until the Secretary of Commerce defines the technical conditions for models and computing clusters subject to the reporting requirements, the Secretary shall require compliance for models and clusters above stated thresholds; section 4.2(c)(iii) provides that, until the Secretary determines the technical conditions for models with potential malicious cyber-enabled capabilities, a stated compute threshold applies; and section 10.1(a) provides that, until agencies designate their permanent Chief AI Officers, they are represented on the interagency council by an Assistant Secretary level official. Each interim command ended on its own terms when the triggering definition, determination or designation occurred, which may precede the 2025-01-20 revocation by EO 14148, and no held source shows whether or when any of those events occurred. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-28 an interval is claimed only when evidence shows the event occurred. In addition the packet inventory of 216 clauses stops at section 10.1 (character 116273 of 146939) and omits the rest of section 10 and sections 11 to 13, so an inventory correction would be needed. Missing sources: held official records dating each trigger (Department of Commerce definition or final rule, the cyber determination, agency Chief AI Officer designations or the OMB guidance under section 10.1(b)), or showing none occurred before 2025-01-20.
